script:
Good morning, Shahriaar. Today is Saturday, November 28. This is your morning brief.

Weather today is 6 degrees Celsius, overcast. The high will be 15 and the low 6 degrees Celsius. Chance of precipitation is 0 percent.

You have 3 appointments in the next 24 hours: 12:00 PM, Logistics system; 1:00 PM, Group Finance Committee; 2:00 PM, Tracking the collection of chain sales receivables.

Now, the top 2 stories in AI today.

First, from WIRED: A New Breed of Chip Runs AI Models Using Waves of Light. German company Q.ANT is developing a new type of chip that runs AI models using waves of light instead of conventional electronics. The approach uses light to perform the most computationally intensive calculations, with the goal of cutting the energy required to run AI models. Why it matters: AI infrastructure and energy efficiency are critical constraints on enterprise AI adoption; a photonic chip that reduces the power needed for model inference could meaningfully change how and where AI models are run.

Second, from The Verge: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun. Google's Android is adding AI-assisted DIY widget creation through Gemini, allowing users to build custom home-screen widgets. One example is a real-time bus arrival widget that alerts users when they are about to miss their bus, eliminating the need to open multiple apps. The feature shows how generative AI is being integrated into everyday mobile productivity, letting people create personalized, context-aware tools directly from the Android home screen. Why it matters: It demonstrates a practical consumer application of generative AI that lets non-developers build useful automated tools, expanding AI's role in daily productivity and mobile workflows.

That is your brief. Have a great day.
